title: Case study: file storage and sync
summary: Chunking, dedupe, metadata vs blob stores, sync conflicts, resumable uploads.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API and data model, high-level design
Deep dives: chunking and dedupe; resumable uploads, integrity and commits; sync and conflicts; durability, hot shares and tiering

labs.title: Storage core: fixed and content-defined chunking, a deduplicating reference-counted chunk store with verification, manifests, resumable upload sessions, exactly-once commit, expiry and GC
Version vectors and conflict resolution with conflicted copies (STRETCH)

outcomes.text: Scope a file storage and sync service in six minutes: the clarifying questions whose answers change the design (sync versus drive, file sizes and networks, edit patterns, sharing, offline edits, sync latency, versions, durability) and non-functional requirements with numbers.

Estimate logical, unique and raw storage (replication versus erasure coding), commit rate, upload bandwidth with and without delta sync, notification fan-out and connections, and metadata size and shard count, and tie each number to a decision.

Design the API and data model: upload sessions with manifests and missing chunks, presigned direct-to-blob uploads, a conditional idempotent commit, a cursor-based change feed; a metadata store sharded by namespace with stable file ids, versions, a journal and shared namespaces, and a content-addressed chunk index.
Draw the high-level design with the upload, download and sync paths traced, notifications published through an outbox as hints, and every box justified by a requirement or a number.

Choose between fixed-size and content-defined chunking and a chunk size from index, manifest and bandwidth arithmetic, and decide the dedupe scope given the existence side channel and hash-as-capability risks.

Design resumable uploads and the commit protocol: durable sessions, idempotent chunk uploads and commits, bytes-first commits, orphan GC with pins and grace periods, and hash verification on write, on read and by a scrubber.

Implement the storage core (labs/c10/chunker): fixed and content-defined chunking with a gear hash, a deduplicating, reference-counted, verifying chunk store, manifests, and resumable upload sessions that accept chunks in any order and in parallel, commit exactly once, expire and are garbage collected, passing under -race.

Design the sync protocol (per-namespace journal and cursors, long-poll or push hints, crash-safe apply, chunk-level delta download) and explain how concurrent edits are detected with base versions or version vectors and resolved with conflicted copies, and when last-writer-wins is acceptable.
Choose between replication and erasure coding and place data across racks and zones, and protect hot shared folders and public links with edge fan-out, jitter, caching and a CDN.
Implement version vectors and conflict resolution (labs/c10/syncvv): compare, merge and decide take, keep or conflicted copy.
Design cold tiering, retention and legal holds, and reason about erasure-coding repair traffic and cross-region layouts with numbers.
